learningObjective: Choose the retirement transition that preserves the stated enrollment and progress behavior.

question.prompt: A course lesson has states Draft, Published, and Retired. Retirement prevents new enrollment, while existing learners keep their progress record linked to the lesson ID. Choose the retirement transition that preserves the stated enrollment and progress behavior.

options.text: Represent retirement as a valid lifecycle transition while preserving the identity needed by existing records.
Have Lesson.retire stop new enrollment and mark the lesson retired without changing its stable ID.
Deletion removes the referent the prompt says existing progress must continue to use.

feedback.reason: Choose the retirement transition that preserves the stated enrollment and progress behavior. Another enrollment path can still accept a learner because the lifecycle state never changed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Another enrollment path can still accept a learner because the lifecycle state never changed.
details.scenarioApplication: The lesson owns its lifecycle status and stable identity; its transition changes availability without erasing the referent.
details.errorCorrection: Delete the lesson row and let progress records recreate it if a learner opens an old course. Keep the lesson published but ask each enrollment screen to hide it from new learners.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Existing progress continues to refer to the same lesson while new enrollment is stopped.
details.transfer: If historical records need a display snapshot, that can be added without replacing the lesson identity.

messages.text: Delete the lesson row and let progress records recreate it if a learner opens an old course.
Keep the lesson published but ask each enrollment screen to hide it from new learners.

learningObjective: Choose how a room move should handle one accepted input and one rejected input.

question.prompt: A studio booking may move from Requested to Confirmed only after the room and time are both accepted. A rejected move must leave the previous confirmed slot intact. Choose how a room move should handle one accepted input and one rejected input.

options.text: Have Booking propose the new room and time, then replace the confirmed slot only after both acceptances succeed.
That leaves a mixed slot that was never accepted as a room-and-time pair.
Make a multi-field state transition preserve the old valid state when its preconditions are not all met.

feedback.reason: Choose how a room move should handle one accepted input and one rejected input. The prompt explicitly requires the previous confirmed slot to remain when the move is rejected.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt explicitly requires the previous confirmed slot to remain when the move is rejected.
details.scenarioApplication: Booking owns the confirmed room/time pair and the move transition.
details.errorCorrection: Write the new room immediately, then keep the old time if the time check fails. Clear the existing slot first so no old booking can survive a failed move.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A failed proposal leaves the original pair intact; a successful one replaces both fields together.
details.transfer: If the system later permits partial holds, represent that as a separate state with its own meaning.

messages.text: Write the new room immediately, then keep the old time if the time check fails.
Clear the existing slot first so no old booking can survive a failed move.

learningObjective: Choose the transition after an export attempt reports a failure.

question.prompt: A whiteboard session can be Open, Closing, or Closed. Export is available only after all accepted strokes are included; a failed export keeps the session Closing and retryable. Choose the transition after an export attempt reports a failure.

options.text: The state claims completion even though the required export did not complete.
Use an explicit intermediate state when completion depends on a fallible operation.
Leave the session in Closing and permit export retry; mark Closed only after a complete export is confirmed.

feedback.reason: Choose the transition after an export attempt reports a failure. That makes it unclear whether a retry should include strokes added after closing began.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That makes it unclear whether a retry should include strokes added after closing began.
details.scenarioApplication: The session owns the lifecycle that gates edits and export completion.
details.errorCorrection: Mark the session Closed before export starts, then discard it if the writer fails. Return the session to Open after failure and allow new strokes to arrive.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A retry continues the same closing attempt without admitting post-close strokes.
details.transfer: If export is optional, the state machine can be simpler; this prompt makes it a close precondition.

messages.text: Return the session to Open after failure and allow new strokes to arrive.
Mark the session Closed before export starts, then discard it if the writer fails.

learningObjective: Choose how to handle a transfer when Queue B has not acknowledged it yet.

question.prompt: An escalation transfers a case from Agent A to Queue B. Queue B must acknowledge the transfer before Agent A releases ownership; the response deadline remains unchanged. Choose how to handle a transfer when Queue B has not acknowledged it yet.

options.text: Preserve the current valid owner until the new owner has accepted the responsibility.
Keep Agent A as owner while the transfer is pending, and change owner only after Queue B acknowledges.
There is a period with no responsible owner, contrary to the required acknowledgement handoff.

feedback.reason: Choose how to handle a transfer when Queue B has not acknowledged it yet. The prompt says the deadline remains unchanged, so delay cannot alter it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt says the deadline remains unchanged, so delay cannot alter it.
details.scenarioApplication: The case owns the current assignment and deadline; transfer is a guarded ownership transition.
details.errorCorrection: Clear Agent A as soon as the transfer request is sent and wait for Queue B to notice it. Extend the response deadline while the transfer is pending.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The case always has an accountable owner, and successful handoff preserves the existing deadline.
details.transfer: A queue may reject the handoff; the case can remain with Agent A until a valid destination accepts.

messages.text: Clear Agent A as soon as the transfer request is sent and wait for Queue B to notice it.
Extend the response deadline while the transfer is pending.

learningObjective: Choose the publish behavior when the stock count is negative.

question.prompt: A produce listing can be Draft or Published. Publishing requires a nonnegative price and stock count; failed validation must leave the draft editable. Choose the publish behavior when the stock count is negative.

options.text: Reject publication and leave the listing Draft with its entered fields available for correction.
The public state is reached before the stated publication condition is checked.
Validate transition preconditions before changing a draft into a published state.

feedback.reason: Choose the publish behavior when the stock count is negative. The prompt says the draft remains editable; clearing input destroys useful draft state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt says the draft remains editable; clearing input destroys useful draft state.
details.scenarioApplication: Listing owns its status and the fields that determine whether publication is allowed.
details.errorCorrection: Set the listing Published, then hide it if a later page notices the negative stock. Erase the entered stock count when validation fails.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A corrected draft can be submitted again without inventing a partially published state.
details.transfer: A separate moderation state is only needed if the product actually distinguishes pending review.

messages.text: Set the listing Published, then hide it if a later page notices the negative stock.
Erase the entered stock count when validation fails.

learningObjective: Choose what approval should do when one requested quantity exceeds delivery.

question.prompt: A return request lists item quantities already delivered. Approval is allowed only when each requested quantity is at most the delivered quantity; rejection leaves the request editable. Choose what approval should do when one requested quantity exceeds delivery.

options.text: That changes the customer’s requested return instead of reporting that its precondition failed.
Guard approval using the state facts that bound the transition.
Reject approval while preserving the editable request so the quantity can be corrected.

feedback.reason: Choose what approval should do when one requested quantity exceeds delivery. Approval has already accepted a quantity the prompt explicitly says must not exceed delivery.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Approval has already accepted a quantity the prompt explicitly says must not exceed delivery.
details.scenarioApplication: ReturnRequest owns the requested lines and the delivered quantities used by the guard.
details.errorCorrection: Approve the lines that fit and silently remove the excess quantity from the other line. Approve the full request and reconcile the excess during refund calculation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The request remains correctable and no return is approved with an over-delivered quantity.
details.transfer: If partial approval is a product behavior, it needs an explicit result the customer can review.

messages.text: Approve the full request and reconcile the excess during refund calculation.
Approve the lines that fit and silently remove the excess quantity from the other line.

learningObjective: Choose how to respond when Plot B becomes occupied before the transfer commits.

question.prompt: A garden plot reservation moves from Plot A to Plot B. Plot B must be vacant at commit time; a denied transfer must preserve Plot A and its approval history. Choose how to respond when Plot B becomes occupied before the transfer commits.

options.text: Guard a transfer against the current destination state and preserve the source assignment on failure.
Keep the reservation on Plot A and reject the transfer because Plot B is no longer vacant.
That violates the stated vacancy precondition and overwrites another active reservation.

feedback.reason: Choose how to respond when Plot B becomes occupied before the transfer commits. A failed transfer is required to preserve the Plot A reservation and its approval history.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A failed transfer is required to preserve the Plot A reservation and its approval history.
details.scenarioApplication: The reservation owns the current plot and transfer history; the destination is checked before changing that state.
details.errorCorrection: Move the reservation anyway and displace the newer Plot B reservation. Remove the reservation from Plot A first, then ask the steward to choose another destination later.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A denied transfer has no partial effect, while a later attempt can use another vacant plot.
details.transfer: If the business supports a temporary unassigned state, it must be specified separately.

messages.text: Move the reservation anyway and displace the newer Plot B reservation.
Remove the reservation from Plot A first, then ask the steward to choose another destination later.

learningObjective: Choose what activation should do if the third component is no longer active.

question.prompt: A regional bundle is Draft until all three component offers are active for the chosen region. Component availability can change while the draft is being reviewed. Choose what activation should do if the third component is no longer active.

options.text: Keep the bundle Draft and report the unavailable component; activate only when all three are active.
The component can change during review, so the old check does not satisfy the activation condition.
Recheck all required member states at the activation boundary.

feedback.reason: Choose what activation should do if the third component is no longer active. That changes the defined bundle instead of satisfying its all-three-components condition.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That changes the defined bundle instead of satisfying its all-three-components condition.
details.scenarioApplication: Bundle owns its component selection and the activation transition checks the required current states.
details.errorCorrection: Activate the bundle from the earlier review result and let checkout discover the missing component. Remove the third component automatically and publish a two-component bundle.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: No customer can see an active bundle whose selected component is unavailable.
details.transfer: If a component can be optional, model that selection explicitly before activation.

messages.text: Activate the bundle from the earlier review result and let checkout discover the missing component.
Remove the third component automatically and publish a two-component bundle.

learningObjective: Choose the state when the expiry instant passes and no vehicle connected.

question.prompt: A charging controller records a connector as Available, Reserved, or Charging. A reservation expires at its stated instant unless a vehicle has connected. Choose the state when the expiry instant passes and no vehicle connected.

options.text: That leaves an expired reservation consuming a state the prompt says should be released.
Apply the lifecycle’s explicit expiry transition based on stored status and time.
Change the connector from Reserved to Available when its reservation expires without connection.

feedback.reason: Choose the state when the expiry instant passes and no vehicle connected. A reservation without a connection is not evidence that charging began.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A reservation without a connection is not evidence that charging began.
details.scenarioApplication: Connector state and its reservation expiry govern the transition.
details.errorCorrection: Keep it Reserved until an operator manually clears it. Change it directly to Charging because the reserved driver may arrive later.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The resource becomes available for another valid reservation after the deadline.
details.transfer: A late arrival may request a new reservation; it does not revive the expired one implicitly.

messages.text: Change it directly to Charging because the reserved driver may arrive later.
Keep it Reserved until an operator manually clears it.

learningObjective: Choose how to commit the merge without losing the source descriptions.

question.prompt: A photo archive merges two metadata records for the same asset. The curator selects the winning title, while both original source descriptions must remain inspectable. Choose how to commit the merge without losing the source descriptions.

options.text: Transition the aggregate to a merged state while retaining explicitly preserved history.
Store the selected title as current metadata and retain both original descriptions as merge provenance.
The prompt requires the originals to remain inspectable, so replacement destroys required history.

feedback.reason: Choose how to commit the merge without losing the source descriptions. The merge would not establish one selected current title as requested.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The merge would not establish one selected current title as requested.
details.scenarioApplication: The archive record owns the selected current metadata and the source history for this merge.
details.errorCorrection: Replace both source descriptions with the winning title after the merge. Keep both metadata records active and make each screen choose whichever title it prefers.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The result has one current title while the two prior descriptions remain auditable.
details.transfer: If provenance is stored in a separate immutable record, that is still part of the merge transition’s result.

messages.text: Replace both source descriptions with the winning title after the merge.
Keep both metadata records active and make each screen choose whichever title it prefers.

learningObjective: Choose how to handle a request to change the territory of an approved permit.

question.prompt: A machine-use permit moves from Draft to Approved only when both territory and expiry are present. Once approved, those fields cannot be edited; a correction requires a new draft. Choose how to handle a request to change the territory of an approved permit.

options.text: Keep the approved permit unchanged and create a new draft for the corrected territory.
The approval would now refer to a territory that was never reviewed.
Represent post-approval correction as a new lifecycle path when the approved record is immutable.

feedback.reason: Choose how to handle a request to change the territory of an approved permit. The prompt requires approved fields to remain unchanged, not the approval history to disappear.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt requires approved fields to remain unchanged, not the approval history to disappear.
details.scenarioApplication: Permit owns its lifecycle state and the fields reviewed at approval.
details.errorCorrection: Edit the territory on the approved permit and keep its old approval timestamp. Erase the permit and its approval history before creating the corrected one.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The existing decision remains accurate, while the correction can receive its own review.
details.transfer: If revocation is needed, model revocation explicitly rather than rewriting the approved record.

messages.text: Edit the territory on the approved permit and keep its old approval timestamp.
Erase the permit and its approval history before creating the corrected one.

learningObjective: Choose the result when the proposed replacement is incompatible.

question.prompt: A drone maintenance job assigns a replacement battery to one aircraft. The old battery must be returned to Available only after the new battery passes the aircraft’s compatibility check. Choose the result when the proposed replacement is incompatible.

options.text: The aircraft loses its valid assignment even though no replacement can be made.
Keep a coupled replacement transition from releasing the current resource until the new one is valid.
Reject the replacement and leave the current battery assignment unchanged.

feedback.reason: Choose the result when the proposed replacement is incompatible. That makes the assignment state contradict the compatibility result.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That makes the assignment state contradict the compatibility result.
details.scenarioApplication: MaintenanceJob owns the replacement attempt; assignment changes only after its compatibility precondition succeeds.
details.errorCorrection: Release the current battery first, then report that the new battery is incompatible. Record the incompatible battery as installed but mark the job incomplete.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A failed replacement leaves the aircraft and old battery in their prior state.
details.transfer: A separate diagnostic record can explain the failed proposal without changing the assignment.

messages.text: Record the incompatible battery as installed but mark the job incomplete.
Release the current battery first, then report that the new battery is incompatible.

learningObjective: Choose the transition after consent has been revoked but before dispatch.

question.prompt: A referral moves from Ready to Sent only when consent is active at dispatch. If consent is revoked before dispatch, no specialist receives the referral. Choose the transition after consent has been revoked but before dispatch.

options.text: Recheck a required authorization at the moment an external transition occurs.
Keep the referral Ready or mark it blocked; do not transition to Sent or disclose it.
Queueing is not dispatch, and the prompt requires consent at the actual disclosure boundary.

feedback.reason: Choose the transition after consent has been revoked but before dispatch. Even a minimal external disclosure is prohibited by the stated no-send condition.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Even a minimal external disclosure is prohibited by the stated no-send condition.
details.scenarioApplication: Referral state and consent status jointly determine whether dispatch is allowed.
details.errorCorrection: Mark it Sent when the care navigator queued it, then suppress future status updates. Send the referral without details so the specialist can request the missing information.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Revocation before dispatch prevents any external recipient from receiving the referral.
details.transfer: If consent is restored later, dispatch can be reconsidered under the then-current state.

messages.text: Mark it Sent when the care navigator queued it, then suppress future status updates.
Send the referral without details so the specialist can request the missing information.

learningObjective: Choose how a late submission should be recorded.

question.prompt: A timed exercise attempt changes from InProgress to Submitted. The submitted attempt pins its exercise revision and scoring policy; late submission is allowed but marked late. Choose how a late submission should be recorded.

options.text: Submit the attempt with its pinned revision and policy and mark its result late.
The prompt explicitly permits late submission; rejection would remove a valid outcome.
Apply the stated transition result without changing the attempt’s pinned interpretation.

feedback.reason: Choose how a late submission should be recorded. That replaces the policy the attempt pinned when it began.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That replaces the policy the attempt pinned when it began.
details.scenarioApplication: Attempt owns its submission state and pinned interpretation.
details.errorCorrection: Reject the attempt because its deadline passed. Rescore it using the policy currently published when the learner submits.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Late status is recorded while the submitted work remains scored under its original policy.
details.transfer: A new attempt may use a newer revision; this attempt does not change retroactively.

messages.text: Reject the attempt because its deadline passed.
Rescore it using the policy currently published when the learner submits.

learningObjective: Choose what a delegate’s approval action should do.

question.prompt: A procurement exception moves to Approved only after the named manager signs it. A delegate may prepare the request but cannot approve it. Choose what a delegate’s approval action should do.

options.text: Preparation completeness does not satisfy the stated signer requirement.
Enforce the actor precondition at the transition that grants approval.
Leave the exception Pending until the named manager signs.

feedback.reason: Choose what a delegate’s approval action should do. That changes who is authorized rather than applying the given transition rule.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That changes who is authorized rather than applying the given transition rule.
details.scenarioApplication: Exception state changes only through a signature from the named manager.
details.errorCorrection: Mark it Approved because the delegate completed all required form fields. Replace the named manager with the delegate in the approval record.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The delegate can prepare but cannot create an approval state.
details.transfer: If delegation authority is later granted, it must be an explicit authorization fact.

messages.text: Replace the named manager with the delegate in the approval record.
Mark it Approved because the delegate completed all required form fields.

learningObjective: Choose how to handle an incomplete annotation mapping result.

question.prompt: A podcast episode replaces a source recording. Existing annotations use time offsets into the old recording; a mapping tool may fail to map some annotations, and failed replacement must leave the old episode playable. Choose how to handle an incomplete annotation mapping result.

options.text: Keep a replacement pending until its dependent state can satisfy the replacement contract.
Keep the old recording active and report the replacement as incomplete until every required annotation maps.
That loses annotations while presenting the replacement as complete.

feedback.reason: Choose how to handle an incomplete annotation mapping result. A mapping failure then leaves no playable episode, contrary to the stated fallback.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A mapping failure then leaves no playable episode, contrary to the stated fallback.
details.scenarioApplication: Episode owns the active recording and its annotation set; replacement changes them as one accepted version.
details.errorCorrection: Activate the new recording and drop annotations the mapper could not place. Delete the old recording before running the mapping tool.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A partial mapping failure leaves the previous playable state intact for retry.
details.transfer: If some annotations are optional, identify that policy before treating a partial result as success.

messages.text: Activate the new recording and drop annotations the mapper could not place.
Delete the old recording before running the mapping tool.

learningObjective: Choose how denial should affect the pending grant.

question.prompt: A temporary role grant moves from Pending to Active only after the reviewer approves it. Its expiry remains scheduled from the approved start time; denial leaves an audit record. Choose how denial should affect the pending grant.

options.text: Transition the grant to Denied and retain the decision record; do not expose the role as active.
The prompt requires an audit record of the denial.
Use a distinct terminal outcome that records denial without making the authority active.

feedback.reason: Choose how denial should affect the pending grant. That creates an interval of authority despite the reviewer denying it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: That creates an interval of authority despite the reviewer denying it.
details.scenarioApplication: Grant owns its lifecycle and decision record; Active is reachable only through approval.
details.errorCorrection: Delete the pending grant so the user can no longer see what was decided. Transition it to Active and immediately schedule a revoke.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A denied grant remains explainable and never provides the permission.
details.transfer: A later request should have a new review identity rather than altering the denied decision.

messages.text: Delete the pending grant so the user can no longer see what was decided.
Transition it to Active and immediately schedule a revoke.

learningObjective: Choose what to do when the document changes after confirmation but before sealing.

question.prompt: A notarization request seals a document revision only after the signer confirms the displayed digest. A changed revision has a different digest. Choose what to do when the document changes after confirmation but before sealing.

options.text: The confirmation is for a different digest, even though the document identity stayed the same.
Guard an irreversible transition with the exact state version that was confirmed.
Do not seal; require confirmation of the changed revision’s digest.

feedback.reason: Choose what to do when the document changes after confirmation but before sealing. The prompt does not authorize silently discarding the newer document state.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The prompt does not authorize silently discarding the newer document state.
details.scenarioApplication: The seal transition binds to a confirmed revision digest.
details.errorCorrection: Seal the latest revision using the earlier confirmation because the document ID is unchanged. Restore the earlier revision silently and seal that revision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: No seal can claim a signer confirmed content they did not see.
details.transfer: A user can review and confirm the new revision to continue.

messages.text: Restore the earlier revision silently and seal that revision.
Seal the latest revision using the earlier confirmation because the document ID is unchanged.

learningObjective: Choose how to handle a timeout when the release outcome is not yet visible to the caller.

question.prompt: A seller payout moves from Ready to Released after settlement. A release request may be retried after a timeout; the payment provider returns the same transfer reference for a repeated request ID. Choose how to handle a timeout when the release outcome is not yet visible to the caller.

options.text: Make a retry converge on the same transition rather than creating another release.
Retry with the same payout request ID and reconcile the returned transfer reference before reporting Released.
A second identity can request a second transfer while the first result is unknown.

feedback.reason: Choose how to handle a timeout when the release outcome is not yet visible to the caller. A timeout does not prove the provider completed the release.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A timeout does not prove the provider completed the release.
details.scenarioApplication: Payout owns its release state and stable request identity; the provider reference resolves the attempt.
details.errorCorrection: Create a new request ID so the provider can attempt the payout again immediately. Mark the payout Released as soon as the request is sent.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The retry can discover the first release without creating a second one.
details.transfer: If the provider does not guarantee repeated request identity, the scenario needs a different reconciliation contract.

messages.text: Create a new request ID so the provider can attempt the payout again immediately.
Mark the payout Released as soon as the request is sent.
